research_task.title: Scope a runnable slice of Certify compact-localization residual

summary: For one explicitly fixed product-cutoff gauge on R3, a compactly supported curl field exactly localizes the transported shear on a core and has a certified three-component residual under affine strain. This is only an algebraic prerequisite for the unchanged parent task.

value_assessment.novelty: The linked prior contribution established the unlocalized affine-strain shear and amplification law. This result adds an explicit compact vector-potential localization and residual identity, while reproducing the prior shear in the unit-cutoff boundary case; the other supplied artifacts address unrelated questions.
value_assessment.evidence: A classical componentwise derivation is supported by an independent exact-integer polynomial coefficient certificate with 48 and 47 nonzero monomials in the first two residual components, zero in the third, and passing divergence, transport, and boundary checks.
value_assessment.falsifier: Any smooth admissible example with a nonzero difference between direct Euler expansion and the stated component formula, or failure of divergence or exact plateau agreement, overturns the scoped claim.

claims.statement: On R3, for the stated transported primitive, smooth compact product cutoffs, and gauge A=(0,0,phi), the curl field is compactly supported, divergence-free, equals the shear on a cutoff plateau, and has residual F1=Q_y+phi_y phi_xy-phi_x phi_yy, F2=-2 lambda phi_x-Q_x-phi_y phi_xx+phi_x phi_xy, F3=0, where Q=D phi-lambda phi.
claims.evidence_summary: The pointwise derivation is reproduced by exact BigInteger polynomial coefficient comparison on a nontrivial profile, including an adversarial unit-cutoff boundary case.
claims.verification_method: Expand the residual directly, compare every polynomial coefficient, and separately check divergence, primitive transport, and plateau reduction.

limitations: The executable polynomial factors test the differential identity but are not compactly supported; compact support is established analytically.
The shear perturbation is localized but the affine background is not.
No localization scale, amplification schedule, all-derivative bound, or force-smoothness result is supplied.
The result does not meet the parent's requirement for two full independent derivations and does not imply finite-time breakdown.
failed_approaches: The JavaScript checker could not run because its runtime command is unavailable; a detected derivative typo was corrected, but no evidence is attributed to that route.
A universal schedule-dependent statement could not be formed because localization scales and an amplification schedule were not supplied.
next_actions: Introduce spatial localization scales and an amplification schedule, then derive sharp bounds for arbitrary spatial and time derivatives of the residual.
Independently rederive the residual and check compactly supported polynomial-piece cutoff interiors and joins.

proposed_tasks.title: Derive scale-explicit force derivative bounds
proposed_tasks.objective: For the fixed product-cutoff localization, introduce explicit localization and amplification schedules and bound every spatial and time derivative of the full residual with all scale factors shown.
proposed_tasks.rationale: The present slice certifies residual algebra but leaves the parent's schedule-dependent estimates untouched.
proposed_tasks.success_criteria: For every stated spatial multi-index and time-derivative order, give a proved residual bound with explicit cutoff, primitive, strain, and scale dependence sufficient to audit force smoothness.
proposed_tasks.useful_failure_criteria: A proved derivative lower bound incompatible with force smoothness for fully specified amplification and localization schedules.
proposed_tasks.verification_method: Differentiate the certified formula, audit product and chain-rule scale powers term by term, and test sharpness on explicit profiles.

proposed_tasks.title: Independently audit the compact-localization residual
proposed_tasks.objective: Produce a second componentwise derivation from direct coordinates and exact checks using compactly supported polynomial-piece cutoff profiles, including join regularity.
proposed_tasks.rationale: This addresses the parent's independent-derivation and cutoff-check dependency without duplicating the derivative-bound task.
proposed_tasks.success_criteria: A second derivation agrees in every component, exact checks pass on each polynomial piece, and claimed regularity across joins is verified.
proposed_tasks.useful_failure_criteria: An explicit component mismatch, missing join regularity, or gauge-dependent term absent from the current formula.
proposed_tasks.verification_method: Compare direct coordinate expansion against the saved formula coefficientwise on all pieces and audit one-sided derivatives at every join.
